scenario: AITA for massaging my guy friend in front of his girlfriend? | I (32F) met my friend (30M) at work last year. We both quit our jobs and became close friends, he introduced me straight away to his girlfriend and this girl is a gem. We hang out a lot the three of us and I love both of them now, even if I knew him first. Today, we were hanging out at the beach for the fireworks and my guy friend was in a bad mood. I asked him what was wrong and he said he had a bad headache. I asked him if he wanted me to give him a head massage because I usually give massages to my friends & family. However, he's pretty tall so I couldn't give it to him while sitting. He then put his head on my laps and I was massaging his head while talking to his girlfriend. I didn't realise it was an uncomfortable situation before seeing the girlfriend's face, which was a bit sceptical. I then quickly put an end to it and sat back at my place. I'm scared I made her mad, even if she was super nice to me the rest of the evening, I find myself completely stupid for not realising it would be super awkward. By the way, I'm dating someone else and I often tell them about my dates and all, so there is absolutely no ambiguity between me & him, and I always see them together, they're a package and I love it. Was I being an asshole here?

prediction.raw: I’ll answer this with a **0** (not an asshole, but the situation was awkward and could have been handled better). ### **Why?** 1. **No Malicious Intent** – You didn’t do anything intentionally disrespectful. Your actions were purely friendly (massaging a stressed friend), and you’ve made it clear you see them as a couple. There’s no deception or hidden romantic interest. 2. **Awkwardness ≠ Assholeness** – The girlfriend’s reaction was likely due to the unexpected nature of the situation, not your character. Many people would find it odd to be massaged in front of their partner, regardless of the context. 3. **Context Matters** – Since you’re in a committed relationship and have been open about your friendship, the girlfriend probably understood the dynamic. Her initial skepticism might have been more about the *moment* than you personally. ### **What Could Have Been Better?** - **Avoiding the Situation** – Since you knew he was stressed, you could’ve suggested a private moment (e.g., *"Want me to give you a quick massage when we’re alone?"*). - **Reading the Room** – Even if you didn’t realize it was awkward, a quick check-in (*"Is this okay for you?"*) would’ve been considerate. - **Clarifying Boundaries** – Since you’re close with the couple, a lighthearted *"Hey, I’m just giving him a quick rub—no weird vibes, right?"* might’ve eased tension. ### **Final Thought** You weren’t an asshole—just a little socially unaware. The girlfriend’s reaction was more about the *moment* than you. Moving forward, being more mindful of boundaries (even if they’re just awkward) will help!
